TAX-001.notes: India GST is the first jurisdiction module. Other countries are not started.

TAX-005.notes: Registration (GSTIN format + check character), GST rates with categories (taxable, nil-rated, exempt, non-GST), place of supply on every GST document. GSTINs are not verified against the GST portal.

TAX-006.notes: Intra-state supplies: half the rate, rounded on its own, posted to Output/Input CGST.

TAX-007.notes: Intra-state supplies in states: posted to Output/Input SGST/UTGST.

TAX-008.notes: Inter-state supplies and exports (with payment of IGST): full rate to Output/Input IGST.

TAX-009.notes: Charged instead of SGST in union territories without a legislature (04, 26, 31, 35, 38, 97); shares the SGST/UTGST account.

TAX-010.notes: Invoices, credit notes, bills and vendor credits carry place of supply, supplier state, buyer/supplier GSTIN and tax by head; posted GST facts are immutable (DB trigger). Bills and vendor credits can be under reverse charge (the vendor is owed the amount without GST; the tax posts as output liability and input credit), including import of services from a vendor outside India (IGST). No PDF tax invoice layout or e-invoice IRN yet.

TAX-011.notes: 4, 6 or 8 digits, required on every GST line except non-GST. No HSN master or rate lookup; units of measure (UQC) are not tracked.

TAX-012.notes: ITC from bills less vendor credits, including reverse-charge tax and import of services (GSTR-3B 4(A)(2), 4(A)(3), 4(A)(5)), set off per CGST Act s.49/49A and rule 88A; reverse-charge tax is paid in cash (s.49(4)). Blocked credits (s.17(5)), reversals, ITC brought forward and GSTR-2B matching are not modelled.

PAY-001.notes: India payroll slice: employees, salary structures, monthly pay runs, payslips, ledger posting and statutory payments. Approvals, cost allocation, reporting and other countries are not built.

PAY-002.notes: Code, PAN (validated), UAN/ESI numbers, joining and leaving dates, work state, PT category, PF/EPS membership and previous-employer salary for the tax year. Identity fields freeze once a payslip is posted.

PAY-003.notes: Dated monthly structures (from the 1st of a month) with components marked as wages or excluded allowances under the Code on Social Security 2020; revisions are kept as history and a used structure cannot change.

PAY-005.notes: Components pro-rated by paid days; the 50% excluded-allowance add-back decides PF and ESI wages.

PAY-006.notes: Employee PF, ESI, Maharashtra professional tax and TDS on salary (new regime). No voluntary deductions, loans or advances.

PAY-007.notes: Bonuses can be added as one-off earnings on a payslip and are taxed in the month. No statutory bonus (Payment of Bonus Act) calculation.

PAY-011.notes: Loss-of-pay days (whole or half) per payslip, and pro-rating for joining or leaving mid-month. No leave balances or leave module.

PAY-016.notes: Posting a pay run journals gross salary and employer PF/ESI against net pay, PF, ESI, PT and TDS payables; voiding reverses it. Source PAYROLL.

PAY-017.notes: Records net-pay and statutory payments from a bank account with due dates (Dr liability, Cr bank). No bank transfer files, ECR or challan files.

PAY-018.notes: Printable payslip with earnings, deductions, employer contributions, income-tax working and year-to-date figures. No PDF or email delivery.

PAY-025.notes: PF/EPS/EDLI (with the Rs 25,000 ceiling from 17 Sep 2026), ESI, Maharashtra PT and new-regime TDS on salary. Not built: old regime, other states' PT, LWF, gratuity, perquisites. See docs/PAYROLL_INDIA.md.

PAY-026.notes: Every rate is cited to its source in the engine and on the settings page, but the rules have not been reviewed by a payroll professional; that review is required before real use.

TAX-023.notes: India compliance calendar: GST (monthly or QRMP, GSTR-9), TDS/TCS deposits and quarterly statements (Forms 138/140/143), PF, ESI, Maharashtra PT and advance tax, from the organisation set-up. Payments are settled by records in the books; returns are marked filed with the acknowledgement (void-only records). No holiday shifts or notified extensions; see docs/COMPLIANCE_CALENDAR_INDIA.md.

TAX-021.notes: Advance tax instalment dates (15/45/75/100%) are tracked and can be marked paid with the challan. The tax itself is not calculated.

PAY-004.notes: Payroll statutory due dates (PF, ESI, PT, TDS on salary, Form 138) are on the compliance calendar. No pay calendars or pay frequencies other than monthly.

TAX-015.notes: India e-invoicing for B2B invoices and credit notes: INV-01 (schema 1.1) JSON for the IRP, single and bulk; import of the IRP response checked against the document (IRN, seller, buyer, number, type, date, total) with optional RS256 signature check against a user-supplied IRP key; signed QR code drawn; 30-day reporting limit for AATO of Rs 10 crore and above; IRN cancellation recorded within 24 hours; a document with a live IRN cannot be voided (API and trigger). No direct IRP/GSP connection, exports, SEZ, debit notes, B2C QR or e-way bills; see docs/E_INVOICING_INDIA.md.

TAX-027.notes: Followed by design: Talk2Tax submits nothing to a government system. E-invoice JSON is uploaded by the user to the IRP and the IRP's response is imported; GST returns and TDS statements are marked filed by hand. An approved GSP/ASP integration is not built.

TAX-016.notes: India e-way bills for outward supplies on tax invoices: which invoices need one (goods value with GST over Rs 50,000 or a state's own intra-state threshold; services and exempt goods left out; 180-day document limit), the portal's bulk JSON with Part B, validity under Rule 138(10), recording the number, vehicle changes kept in order, cancellation within 24 hours, and no void with a live e-way bill (API and trigger). No portal/GSP connection, exports, inward or job-work movements, extensions or consolidated bills; see docs/E_WAY_BILLS_INDIA.md.

FPA-002.notes: Annual budgets per fiscal year for revenue and expense accounts, as numbered versions (empty, copied, or last year's actuals with a percentage change), with an annual amount spread evenly over the months to the paisa. See docs/BUDGETS.md.

FPA-004.notes: Twelve monthly amounts per account, entered in a grid or spread from an annual amount; quarters are a reporting view only (no entry by quarter). See docs/BUDGETS.md.

FPA-014.notes: Budget vs actual by month, quarter or year against posted journals: variance, percentage and favourable/unfavourable per account and for revenue, expenses and net income, year to date, periods in progress, unbudgeted accounts flagged. No drill-down or export yet.

FPA-023.notes: Submit, withdraw, send back with a reason, approve by someone other than the submitter (API and CHECK); one approved version per year, earlier one superseded; approved versions immutable (triggers). Single approval step.

FPA-008.notes: Daily cash and bank forecast from open invoices and bills at each contact's usual payment delay (last year's settled documents; everyone's history or the due date when fewer than 3), planned receipts and payments (once, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly), a low and high case, a minimum-balance warning, and weekly or monthly buckets. Rule-based, no machine learning. See docs/CASH_FLOW_FORECAST.md.

FPA-024.notes: Saved forecasts are immutable (trigger) and compared day by day with the actual closing cash from posted journals: average miss, bias, share of days inside the range, largest miss. No alerts when accuracy drops.

FPA-029.notes: 30-day horizon of the cash-flow forecast (weekly buckets). Cash only: not a profit or balance sheet forecast.

FPA-030.notes: 60-day horizon of the cash-flow forecast (weekly buckets). Cash only: not a profit or balance sheet forecast.

FPA-031.notes: 90-day horizon of the cash-flow forecast (weekly buckets). Cash only: not a profit or balance sheet forecast.

FPA-032.notes: 180-day horizon of the cash-flow forecast (monthly buckets). Cash only: not a profit or balance sheet forecast.

FPA-033.notes: 365-day horizon of the cash-flow forecast (monthly buckets). Cash only: not a profit or balance sheet forecast.

FPA-035.notes: Backtesting: a forecast rebuilt from the books as they stood on an earlier day (up to 2 years back), saved and measured against actual cash. The range is the 25th to 75th percentile of payment delays, not a statistical confidence interval; backtests use today's planned items. Kept below Tested until a real interval model exists.

FPA-021.notes: 13 KPIs computed monthly from posted journals (revenue, gross/operating/net margin, opex ratio, current and quick ratio, working capital, liabilities to equity, DSO, DPO, net cash flow, runway), each with its formula, components, previous month, same month last year, 13-month history, and a target (at least / at most) that is met or missed. Fixed catalogue: no custom KPI formulas. See docs/KPIS_AND_MANAGEMENT_REPORTS.md.

RPT-019.notes: Financial ratios: margins, operating expense ratio, current and quick ratio, liabilities to equity, DSO and DPO, from posted journals by account subtype, with the figures behind each. DSO/DPO compare GST-inclusive balances with tax-exclusive revenue/expenses (documented).

RPT-018.notes: Working capital (current assets − current liabilities at month end), with current and quick ratio, DSO and DPO and their history. Classification by account subtype; an unclassified liability counts as current.

RISK-012.notes: Revenue by customer from posted invoices less credit notes (tax excluded) over the last 12 months and per month: top 5 with shares, the rest grouped, and a warning when one customer is 40% or more. No alerts or scoring.

RPT-024.notes: Monthly management report: grouped P&L for the month vs previous month, same month last year and the approved budget, year to date, cash, KPIs and top customers, with commentary. Finalising freezes figures and commentary (trigger); later postings are listed against it. Printable from the browser; no PDF export, scheduling or distribution yet.

AR-032.notes: Regular customer not billed: a customer invoiced in each of the previous N months (default 3) with no invoice in the last complete month. Rule-based; no contract or subscription data yet.

RISK-001.notes: Possible duplicate bill (same vendor, same total, within N days, under different invoice numbers) and possible duplicate payment (same vendor, same amount, within N days). The same vendor invoice number is refused at entry (AP-018).

RISK-004.notes: Manual journals posted in the last 90 days that are N times the median manual journal of the year before (with a minimum amount), or posted more than N days after their date.

RISK-018.notes: Every alert stores the figures and records it was raised on (facts, linked records, a table) and the check description; history of every state change.

RISK-019.notes: Alerts are worded as things to check, never as accusations; dismissing needs a reason and is kept in the history and audit trail.

AUDIT-010.notes: Alerts are tracked per finding: open, acknowledged, dismissed (with reason) or cleared when no longer found; reopen on recurrence; append-only history and audit events.

INNOV-005.notes: Nine checks run in the background (ALERTS_RUNNER_INTERVAL_SECONDS, default 300; organisations with posted entries not checked in the last hour, oldest first, 20 a pass), on demand, and when alerts are opened. Every alert has a priority score 0-100 with its reasons (severity, money at stake against average monthly revenue, days open, times it came back, minus 15 when acknowledged) and the list is ordered by it. New and reopened alerts become tasks by a per-organisation setting (critical or warnings, role, due days), closed automatically when the alert clears or is dismissed. No email or push notifications yet.

NAV-004.notes: Copilot screen with saved conversations; answers come from read-only tools over the books (P&L, balance sheet, trial balance, ageing, KPIs, management report, cash-flow forecast, budget vs actual, alerts, compliance calendar) and list the reports used. Runs on Anthropic's Claude API through the official SDK; tested end to end against a local stand-in for the API. Not yet run against the live API: waiting for ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

SEC-032.notes: Copilot: every question and answer is in the audit trail (who, outcome, tools used, model that answered, tokens); answers keep the exact exchange with the model.

AUDIT-016.notes: Copilot conversations keep each answer with the reports it read; finished messages cannot be changed (database trigger).

RULE-005.notes: Without an API key the copilot says it is not set up and sends nothing; it never shows canned answers. Tests use a scripted stand-in model that is never reachable from the app.

RULE-011.notes: The copilot has read-only tools only; a call to any other tool is refused and reported back to the model.

AGENT-060.notes: Organisation-wide emergency stop with a reason (owners and admins), shown in every refusal; every agent checks before each model call, so work already running stops and what it had not reached is marked as not done. Per-agent switches too. Not built: a platform-wide stop across all organisations (only removing the API key does that).

WFLOW-001.notes: Form-based builder: one trigger (an event, a schedule, or a date an invoice or bill reaches), conditions that must all hold, and up to five actions (task, email or webhook). No visual canvas, branches or drag and drop yet.

WFLOW-002.notes: Eight triggers read from the audit trail (a transactional outbox): invoice or bill posted, invoice or bill voided, customer payment, vendor payment, manual journal, expense claim submitted, alert opened. A workflow acts only on events after it is turned on.

WFLOW-004.notes: Runner in the API process (WORKFLOW_RUNNER_INTERVAL_SECONDS) with a per-organisation cursor locked FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; one live run per workflow and event, enforced by a unique index.

WFLOW-005.notes: Conditions on the event’s facts (money, text, date, choice), all of which must hold. No either/or branches yet.

WFLOW-012.notes: POST with JSON, signed HMAC-SHA256 (t2t-signature: t=,v1=), same delivery id and bytes on every retry, 10-second timeout, no redirects. Public https only in production: DNS answers are checked and the connection is pinned to the checked address.

WFLOW-014.notes: Six attempts: retries after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h and 6 h. Webhooks: network errors, timeouts, 408, 429 and 5xx; other answers end the delivery. Emails: no answer or a 4xx SMTP answer; 5xx ends it.

WFLOW-015.notes: Failed runs say which action failed and why; an owner or admin can send a failed webhook or email again from the run log. A task for someone who has left, or an email with no address, fails that action only.

WFLOW-016.notes: A change to trigger, conditions or actions makes a new immutable version (database trigger); runs keep their version; stale edits are refused.

WFLOW-017.notes: Dry run on the latest real event (or a chosen one), the latest time a schedule came round, or a real open invoice or bill: facts, each condition with its actual value, the task and the email each action would make. Webhooks are sent only when asked, marked "test": true; test emails go to the tester only, with [Test] in the subject.

WFLOW-018.notes: Run log per workflow: event, version, conditions, each action with its attempts, answers and timings. Runs and actions are append-only in the database.

INNOV-006.notes: One work queue for tasks from people, automations, the AI assistant (confirmed actions), alerts and the month-end close. Each task records its source (backfilled for earlier tasks), shows it, and the queue filters by it; tasks for a person or a role, due dates, overdue, links to the record, done or cancelled with a note, audit trail. Alert tasks close themselves.

NAV-036.notes: Automations list, builder (events, schedules, dates), test (emails go to the tester only), run log with each email and webhook attempt, versions and webhook signing secret for owners and admins.

WFLOW-003.notes: Three schedule triggers: on a schedule (every day, every week on a weekday, or every month on day 1-28, at a time in India time), an invoice N days overdue, and a bill due in N days. Each acts once per occurrence (unique index on workflow and occurrence), only on times and dates from when it was turned on, so turning one on never sends a backlog. Schedule facts include overdue and outstanding receivables and payables.

WFLOW-009.notes: Email action: plain-text email to everyone with a role, one member, or the customer or vendor on the record, with {{placeholders}}, amounts like ₹1,50,000.00 and dates like 2 Nov 2026. Sent over SMTP (nodemailer, SMTP_URL and EMAIL_FROM) after the run commits, with the webhook retry schedule for 4xx answers or no answer; 5xx is final. Tests send to a local SMTP server; not yet run against a real mail provider. No SMS, chat or in-app notifications.

AR-024.notes: Collection reminders as an automation: "An invoice is overdue" (N days after the due date, still not fully paid) can email the customer and give a task, once per invoice. Waiting on a real SMTP server for a live check. Also AI-drafted reminders with human approval on the Collections page (AR-035). No reminder sequences, escalation by age or tracking of replies yet.

AR-035.notes: The AI model (Anthropic Claude through the copilot model) drafts one plain-text reminder per customer with overdue invoices, from facts worked out from posted invoices, allocations, receipts and earlier reminders. Every amount and invoice number in a draft (or an edit) is checked against those facts, and every overdue invoice must be mentioned; a person must approve and send each one, after the balances are checked again. Tested with a scripted model and a local Messages API stand-in; waiting on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and a real SMTP server for a live check.

AGENT-024.notes: Collections agent: drafting runs (up to 20 customers, most overdue first; customers with no email, a reminder waiting or one sent in the last 7 days are listed as left out), a risk level with reasons per customer, review, edit, reject or send with human approval, delivery retries, and an audit event for every step. It never sends on its own. Waiting on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and real SMTP for a live check.

WFLOW-019.notes: Built: overdue invoices → AI risk assessment → drafted reminder → checks against the books → sent only once a person approves. Not built: tracking replies and a collections dashboard beyond the queue; the AI step is waiting on a live key.

AUDIT-019.notes: AI activity page (Governance): every copilot answer and reminder draft shows the model asked and the model that answered, from the provider response.

AUDIT-026.notes: AI activity page: the outcome of each AI call (answered, declined, failed, drafted) with tokens used, and for reminders what a person decided (sent, sent with edits, rejected, not delivered).

AGENT-004.notes: Bank reconciliation agent: for each unmatched statement line without an exact one-to-one match (up to 25 per run, oldest first), the AI model (Anthropic Claude) suggests ledger lines already in the books that add up to it, a receipt or payment against open invoices or bills, or an entry to one account, with a confidence and a reason. It sees short references, never ids; every proposal is checked against what it was shown; a person accepts or dismisses each, and accepting goes through the same matching, receipt and entry code as by hand. Tested with a scripted model and a local Messages API stand-in; waiting on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for a live check.

BANK-016.notes: Bank lines are classified by the AI model into a match, a receipt or payment for a contact, or an entry to an account from the chart, using how a person booked the last 15 bank lines as examples. Suggestions only; a person accepts each. Waiting on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for a live check.

AUDIT-022.notes: Every AI proposal is kept as proposed (bank suggestions: the action and references the model sent, and the resolved records; reminders: the text the model wrote), frozen by database triggers, next to what a person decided. Month-end close entries keep the lines, reason and confidence the model proposed, frozen the same way.

AUDIT-023.notes: Each AI proposal stores and shows the model's own short reason (bank suggestions) or risk reasons (reminders), with the checks run on it. These are the model's stated reasons, not its internal reasoning. Month-end close entries keep the lines, reason and confidence the model proposed, frozen the same way.

AGENT-005.notes: Month-end closing agent: the AI model (Anthropic Claude) is shown the close checklist and how every account moved in the month against the three months before, points out what looks unusual, and proposes adjusting entries (accruals that reverse next month, prepayment releases, reclasses) using account codes only. Every entry is checked (allowed accounts, balanced, amounts, somewhere open to reverse) and posted only when a person approves it, through the normal journal code. Tested with a scripted model and a local Messages API stand-in; waiting on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for a live check.

WFLOW-021.notes: Built: a checklist worked out from the books (draft journals, unmatched bank lines, trial balance, draft documents, reconciliation, approvals, expense claims, payroll, depreciation, negative cash, AI items waiting, earlier months), tasks for accountants for each open check, an AI review that proposes adjusting entries, approval by a person, closing that locks the period with a certification of the figures, and reopening with a reason. Not built: starting the close automatically as a period ends, and generating the report pack at close.

AUDIT-015.notes: Closing a month records a certification: who closed it and when, the checklist as it stood (with the warnings accepted and the note saying why), and the month's totals (revenue, expenses, net profit, assets, liabilities, trial balance, journals posted). Only owners and admins can close or reopen; a database trigger keeps a certification unchanged except for recording one reopening with its reason, and an unlock on the periods page is refused while the close stands.

AGENT-001.notes: AI control center page: every AI agent (copilot, collections, bank reconciliation, month-end close) with its action level, on/off switch, monthly token budget, usage this month, failures, acceptance rate over 90 days, what is running and waiting, and the organisation-wide emergency stop.

AGENT-052.notes: Acceptance rate per agent over the last 90 days, from what people did with its proposals: reminders sent (with or without edits) or rejected, bank suggestions accepted or dismissed by a person, adjusting entries posted or rejected. Not built: accuracy against a labelled set.

AGENT-053.notes: Tokens in and out tracked per call and per agent per month, with an optional monthly token budget per agent that is enforced before each model call. Not built: converting tokens to money at provider prices.

AGENT-054.notes: The copilot is level 0: it can only run read-only reports; shown in the control center.

AGENT-056.notes: Collections, bank reconciliation and month-end close agents are level 2: they prepare reminders, matches and entries that only take effect when a person approves them. The level is fixed in code, not a setting.

AGENT-044.notes: Each agent run needs the starting member's permission for that feature, the organisation's AI switch, the agent's own switch and its budget, checked again before every model call. Not built: an orchestrator assigning work between agents.

AGENT-046.notes: Running and failed work per agent in the control center; every call in AI activity. Not built: a single cross-agent task model.

ENT-019.notes: Fixed asset register: assets with category, serial number, location, accounts, cost, residual value and dates; purchase posted from the register or already in the books; assets brought in part-depreciated; terms fixed once depreciation is posted (database trigger); disposal with proceeds and gain or loss posted. Not built: asset categories with default terms, transfers between locations, revaluation, impairment, partial disposal, tagging or photos.

ENT-020.notes: Straight-line and written-down-value depreciation by month, posted once a month as one journal (catching up missed months), reversible latest first; schedules per asset. Not tested against a published depreciation schedule (for example Companies Act Schedule II rates); no separate tax-book (Income Tax Act block) depreciation.

NAV-026.notes: Accounting → Fixed assets: register, add or change an asset, asset detail with schedule and disposal, depreciation runs.

ENT-016.notes: Deferred revenue schedules: receipt posted to a liability (2350 Deferred Revenue in the standard chart) or already in the books, released to revenue evenly by month or by days in one monthly journal with catch-up, latest-first reversal, ended early with what is left to revenue or refunded; month-end close warns about unposted releases. Not built: schedules created from invoice lines, recognition by milestone, usage or performance obligation (Ind AS 115 beyond straight-line over time).

ENT-017.notes: Prepaid expense schedules: payment posted to a prepaid account or already in the books, released to expense evenly by month or by days in one monthly journal with catch-up, latest-first reversal, ended early with what is left expensed or moved to a refund account. Not built: schedules created from bill lines, foreign-currency schedules.

ENT-018.notes: Month-end accruals of expense or income: posted on the last day of the month with the automatic reversal on the first day of the next; cancelling posts the opposite entries on both dates. Not built: recurring accruals, other reversal dates, accruals suggested from history (the month-end close AI review can propose accrual entries separately).

ENT-014.notes: Departments and projects as masters (code unique per kind, never deleted, made inactive instead) tagging journal, invoice, credit note, bill and vendor credit lines; tags checked by organisation, kind and active state in the API and by the database, carried from document lines to the journal and kept on reversals. Not built: more than two dimensions, cost allocation across departments, splitting one line across projects.

RPT-027.notes: Profit and loss with a column per department or project plus Not assigned, totals, net profit and margin per column; the profit and loss filtered by department and project. Not built: trial balance, balance sheet, general ledger and budgets by dimension.

GL-026.notes: Departments: code, name, description, active; tag any journal or document line; profit and loss by department.

GL-029.notes: Projects: code, name, customer, start and end dates, active; tag any journal or document line; profit and loss by project. Not built: project budgets, time or billing by project.

GL-024.notes: Departments serve as cost centres: expenses tagged to a department are its costs and the report shows them per department. Not built: a separate cost centre hierarchy, cost allocation rules, cost centre budgets.

RPT-014.notes: Department profitability: revenue, expenses, net profit and margin per department for any date range, with untagged activity under Not assigned.

RPT-013.notes: Project profitability: revenue, expenses, net profit and margin per project for any date range. Not built: budget vs actual per project, work in progress, percentage of completion.

TRS-009.notes: Loans kept as a register: money received posted or brought in from opening balances, installments posted from the bank split into principal and interest, prepayments with charges (shorter term or lower installment), floating-rate changes, reversal of the latest entry, closing when repaid, overdue installments, and what is owed within 12 months and later. Not built: covenants, security, drawdowns in tranches, moratorium periods, foreign-currency loans, loans given (receivable).

TRS-010.notes: Repayment schedules for EMI and equal-principal loans, previewed as the loan is entered, recomputed after prepayments and rate changes, with installments paid and still to pay. Not built: bullet or balloon repayments, quarterly or irregular installments, step-up EMIs.

TRS-011.notes: Interest monthly on the opening balance of each installment period (monthly rests), rounded to the currency; the lender's own split can be recorded instead. Not built: daily-balance interest, interest accrued at month end between installment dates, interest income on deposits.

TRS-016.notes: Treasury overview: cash and bank balances, borrowings (within 12 months and later), net cash or debt, installments due in 30 days and overdue, repayments by month for 12 months, interest paid this financial year, and a check of each loan account in the ledger against the loans. Not built: cash forecast on the same page (see the cash-flow forecast), investments, FX exposure, multi-entity cash pooling.

TRS-002.notes: Cash and bank balances from posted journals up to today, and net cash after borrowings, on the treasury overview. Not built: intraday or bank-fed balances, balances by entity or currency.

BANK-011.notes: Interest on loans is worked out per installment and posted to the interest expense account. Not built: interest earned on bank balances or deposits.

I18N-006.notes: Invoice and credit note layouts from country presets: India GST tax invoice (CGST Rule 46 checks), UAE VAT (bilingual title), UK VAT, US, Singapore GST, Australia GST, EU VAT (Article 226 checks) and generic. Each preset sets the title, tax number label, columns, date and number style, paper size and the rules the designer warns about. Not built: Saudi ZATCA QR, Arabic right-to-left body text, legal review of each preset.

I18N-009.notes: Templates per organisation: five themes, eight palettes plus custom colours, fonts, editable and reorderable sections and columns, logos, and HTML templates with safe placeholders. Covers invoices and credit notes; quotes, statements, receipts and payslips do not use templates yet.

I18N-004.notes: Each person chooses how dates are shown (06 Nov 2026, 06/11/2026, 11/06/2026 or 2026-11-06); month names follow the language. Invoice templates keep their own per-template date style for the printed document.

RPT-033.notes: PDF export of the trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet, general ledger, receivables and payables ageing, and profit by department or project from an Export button on each report page. A4 with landscape for wide reports, header row repeated on every page, bold subtotals and totals with rules, notes, footer with page numbers, lakh/crore grouping for INR. Uses the PDF standard fonts, so characters outside Western European scripts print as '?'. Every export is audited (report.exported) with the file's SHA-256.

RPT-034.notes: Excel (.xlsx) export of the trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet, general ledger, receivables and payables ageing, and profit by department or project. Amounts are real numbers with a currency format (lakh/crore grouping chosen per cell for INR, checked in LibreOffice), dates are Excel dates, frozen header, bold totals, notes. Written without dependencies (stored ZIP). Text is never written as a formula.

RPT-035.notes: CSV export of the trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet, general ledger, receivables and payables ageing, and profit by department or project: UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF, RFC 4180 quoting, amounts as plain decimals, and text that a spreadsheet would run as a formula (=, +, -, @) prefixed with an apostrophe.

ENT-001.notes: Each company is its own organisation with its own books; a user can belong to many and switch between them. Companies owned or administered by the same user can now be grouped under a parent for group reporting (see ENT-007).

ENT-002.notes: Groups of entities owned by a parent organisation: owners and admins add the companies they also own or administer; consolidated reports need report access in every member, and each member's figures are read inside its own tenant context (row-level security applies).

ENT-007.notes: Consolidation worksheet (per company, eliminations, consolidated) and consolidated profit and loss and balance sheet for any period, combined by account code, with CSV/Excel/PDF export audited with the file hash. Full consolidation only (every member treated as 100% owned).

ENT-009.notes: Elimination rules pair one member's account with another's (current accounts, intercompany sales and purchases, investment and share capital), checked against each member's chart of accounts. Both balances are removed; a mismatch stays visible in an 'Intercompany differences to resolve' line and the worksheet still balances. Intercompany balances must sit on dedicated accounts (AR/AP control accounts cannot be split).

ENT-011.notes: Members in another currency are translated with user-entered rates per period end: assets and liabilities at closing, revenue and expenses at average, equity and earnings brought forward at a historical rate, with the difference in a foreign currency translation reserve. Rates are not fetched from a market source.

ENT-012.notes: Group reporting through consolidation groups: worksheet, consolidated P&L and balance sheet, elimination status and translation summary on one page, exportable.

evidence: apps/web group consolidation page: share column, split lines
ENT-010.notes: Outside share of the subsidiary's reported net assets and profit; no goodwill, fair value adjustments or indirect holdings. See docs/CONSOLIDATION.md.

ENT-008.notes: Charges and settlements posted in both companies in one database transaction, reversed together, and eliminated by their exact amounts. Journals only: no GST/VAT, stock or unrealised profit.

TWIN-002.notes: Monthly driver model built from the last 3, 6 or 12 months of posted figures: revenue as volume x price x exchange rate, cost of sales following volume, payroll, other costs, receivables and payables days, cash, and tax.

TWIN-003.notes: Revenue growth per month, from a chosen month.

TWIN-004.notes: Expense change by percentage and/or monthly amount on operating costs, payroll or cost of sales.

TWIN-005.notes: People, monthly cost each, one-off cost each, from a month.

TWIN-006.notes: One-off cost, running cost, and revenue ramping to full speed.

TWIN-007.notes: Price change with a volume response; cost of sales follows volume, not price.

TWIN-008.notes: Income tax rate on profit before tax; losses get no relief (documented simplification). Rate comes from the scenario, else history, else none (asked for).

TWIN-009.notes: New loan repaid by EMI from the month after; interest through profit, principal through cash.

TWIN-010.notes: Asset purchase depreciated straight-line from the month after.

TWIN-011.notes: Supplier cost change on cost of sales.

TWIN-013.notes: Share of revenue in foreign currency and a rate change.

TWIN-014.notes: Revenue drop and slower collections, for a number of months or for good.

TWIN-016.notes: Collection and payment days changes, flowing through receivables and payables.

TWIN-017.notes: Gaps listed as Inputs to confirm: no tax rate (none in the scenario or history), no revenue in the baseline, no inflation over horizons beyond 12 months, and no investment when hiring five or more people.

TWIN-018.notes: Each missing input is asked as a question, with an Add button for the change it needs.

TWIN-019.notes: Nine ready-made templates plus a builder with 15 kinds of change. Templates are fixed placeholder figures, not AI-generated.

TWIN-020.notes: Monthly projection of revenue, costs, EBITDA, depreciation, interest, tax, net profit, cash flow and closing cash.

TWIN-021.notes: Lowest cash, the month cash runs out, and cash to raise to stay above the buffer.

TWIN-022.notes: Net profit and margin over the horizon, and break-even month.

TWIN-023.notes: Rule-based risks, each High/Medium/Low: cash runs out (with the amount to raise), cash below the buffer, a loss over the horizon, ending loss-making, thin gross margin, growing receivables, weak loan-payment cover, and a short history.

TWIN-024.notes: Up to five saved scenarios side by side with no change, same baseline and horizon.

TWIN-025.notes: Every change and baseline figure explained in words in the Assumptions list.

TWIN-026.notes: Saved per organisation with name, description, baseline and horizon; re-run against the latest actuals on every open; audited.

TWIN-027.notes: Scenarios are stored only as inputs in twin_scenarios; nothing posts to the ledger (API and browser tests count journals before and after).

TWIN-028.notes: Actual months solid, hypothetical dashed over a shaded band, every projected figure labelled hypothetical. The separate cash-flow forecast stays on its own page and is not overlaid here.

INTG-032.notes: Each organisation sets up its own SMTP server (any provider offering SMTP) in Settings → Integrations, with a test that signs in and sends an email. Tested against a local SMTP server; waiting on a check with a real provider.

INTG-034.notes: Each organisation adds its own Claude API key and model in Settings → Integrations; all four AI agents use it. Tested through the official SDK against a local stand-in; waiting on a check with a live key.

INTG-040.notes: For AI and email: which settings are in use (the organisation’s, the server’s fallback, or none) and the last test result with its message, time and who ran it.

INTG-047.notes: Creating, changing, testing and removing an integration are audited; secrets are never written to the audit trail, only whether they changed and their last four characters.

INTG-048.notes: Each integration can be switched off (kept) or removed; the features then fall back to the server’s settings or say they are not set up.

INTG-050.notes: The page shows "Not tested", "Working" or "Failed" from a real test, never "connected" just because settings were saved; the registry keeps Claude and email at Integration pending until checked with live credentials.

NAV-039.notes: Governance → Integrations, for owners and admins (org.manage).

WAR-001.notes: One page per scenario where the team works together: model, impacts, suggestions, notes, versions and approval. Not live: others see changes on reload, with no presence or live cursors.

WAR-002.notes: Up to five saved scenarios side by side with the no-change baseline, now with approval status and a risk map.

WAR-003.notes: Driver-based monthly simulations played forward from the posted books (see the digital twin).

WAR-004.notes: Monthly closing cash, lowest cash, cash to raise and the month cash runs out, for every scenario.

WAR-005.notes: Planning board: scenarios in Draft, Waiting for approval, Approved and Rejected columns, with version, open notes and who submitted or decided.

WAR-006.notes: Risk map on the comparison page: each risk the engine finds, by scenario, with its level and details.

WAR-008.notes: Each change can belong to a department; the war room shows the measured net profit and cash effect of each change and the total by department.

WAR-009.notes: Investment changes (equipment bought and depreciated) and new loans in scenarios.

WAR-010.notes: Expansion changes: one-off cost, running costs and revenue ramping up to full speed.

WAR-011.notes: Notes on a scenario, optionally pinned to a projected month and a change, recorded against the version; resolve by the author or a scenario manager, delete by the author; open notes counted on the board.

WAR-012.notes: Submit, withdraw, approve, reject (with a reason) and reopen; frozen while waiting or approved; the submitter cannot decide; new permission scenarios.approve (owners, admins, approvers); every step audited.

WAR-013.notes: Every saved set of inputs is an immutable version with who and why; restoring makes an earlier version the newest.

WAR-014.notes: Left column: scenario settings and the changes, each with its department.

WAR-015.notes: Centre: the projection updating as changes are typed, chart, risks, inputs to confirm, impacts and month table.

WAR-016.notes: Suggested next moves (fund the gap, collect sooner, price rise, delay the largest cost, set the tax rate) measured by re-running the model, plus risks and assumptions in words. Rule-based, not written by AI yet.

WAR-017.notes: Compare up to five scenarios at once.

RECOV-001.notes: Recovery workspace: options from the books, plans with owners, due dates, status and notes, liquidity forecast, and copying into a twin scenario. Rule-based, not AI-assisted yet.

RECOV-002.notes: Spending freeze option (other operating costs -10%) measured on the twin.

RECOV-003.notes: Chase overdue invoices (up to 90 days late counted as recoverable, customers listed largest first) and shorter terms for new invoices.

RECOV-004.notes: A 20% cut option for each of the five largest operating expense accounts, from their average monthly spend.

RECOV-005.notes: Longer payment terms and 3% lower prices from suppliers, listing suppliers by average monthly bills.

RECOV-006.notes: Working capital loan sized until its repayments no longer open a gap, and new capital from owners or investors.

RECOV-007.notes: Price rise option (+5% with 2% less volume).

RECOV-008.notes: Payroll cost reduction modelled only, marked as a decision for the owners, never a recommendation to let anyone go.

RECOV-009.notes: Liquidity forecast of the plan against no action: runway, lowest cash, cash still to raise, month-end cash chart.

RECOV-010.notes: Each option and the plan show measured outcomes (lowest cash, cash at the end, net profit, whether cash runs out) and risks.

RECOV-011.notes: The planner only records decisions: tests check no journal, payment or loan is created; options needing a decision are marked.

VCFO-001.notes: Virtual CFO built: health score, nine analyses, nine worked questions, board packs and investor updates with a checked AI summary. Peer benchmarking and configurable thresholds are not built.

VCFO-002.notes: Health score out of 100 from five stated rules (liquidity, profitability, working capital, growth, solvency) with a grade.

VCFO-003.notes: Deterministic headline on every assessment; AI executive summary of packs written from the facts and rejected if it quotes any figure not in them. Tested against the scripted model and the local stand-in; needs a live check with a Claude key.

VCFO-004.notes: Recommendations from areas needing action, then watch, with priority, link and required approval.

VCFO-005.notes: Liquidity: cash, current and quick ratios, monthly change in cash, runway, 90-day forecast lowest point against the minimum balance.

VCFO-006.notes: Profitability: revenue, gross, operating and net profit and margins over three months against the previous three and last year.

VCFO-007.notes: Working capital: DSO, DPO, days inventory, cash conversion cycle, overdue receivables.

VCFO-008.notes: Revenue growth: three months against the three before and last year, 12 against the 12 before, largest customer share.

VCFO-009.notes: Cost reduction: expense lines up more than 15% on the six months before, with the monthly saving and who approves a cut.

VCFO-010.notes: Risk detection: runway, forecast below minimum, losses, negative equity, interest cover, concentration, overdue filings, high alerts.

VCFO-011.notes: Scenario analysis: 10% salary rise measured on the digital twin; planning section counts saved, approved and waiting scenarios; links to the twin and war room.

VCFO-012.notes: Board packs: every area, recommendations, commentary, checked AI summary, refresh while draft, finalise (immutable at the database level), print.

VCFO-013.notes: Investor updates: growth, profitability, liquidity, capital and debt, with the same commentary, summary and finalise.

VCFO-014.notes: Planning: year-to-date variance against the approved budget and scenario status, with a prompt to prepare a budget.

VCFO-015.notes: Capital allocation: free cash above a reserve of three months of fixed costs or the minimum balance, with options and approvals.

VCFO-016.notes: Expansion: months an expansion adding a fifth to fixed costs could be funded from free cash, with a link to the twin expansion template.

VCFO-017.notes: Debt: loans outstanding, principal and interest due in 12 months, interest cover, debt service cover, liabilities to equity.

VCFO-018.notes: Compares with the organisation's own history (previous months, same months last year) only; peer and industry benchmarks are the benchmarking module.

VCFO-019.notes: Why profit changed (fell or rose) last month: accounts by their effect on profit.

VCFO-020.notes: Clients ranked by revenue, share, change, overdue and days late. Costs are not recorded per client, so profit per client is not known; the answer says so with low confidence.

VCFO-021.notes: Projects with a net loss over 12 months from profit by project.

VCFO-022.notes: Cash needed next quarter: minimum balance minus the 90-day forecast lowest point, base and late cases, plus the twin trend.

VCFO-023.notes: Expenses to investigate: accounts more than 25% above their six-month average, plus duplicate and unusual-journal alerts.

VCFO-024.notes: Salaries +10%: twin with and without, profit, cash and runway.

VCFO-025.notes: Vendors charging more: unit price by vendor and item, last 90 days against the 9 months before, with extra cost.

BENCH-001.notes: Opt-in network: owners and admins join with recorded, versioned consent and can withdraw at any time.

BENCH-002.notes: Give-to-get: each shared metric is compared with the median and quartiles of peer groups (industry, size, country), narrowest group with enough participants first.

BENCH-005.notes: Revenue growth, 12 months against the 12 before.

BENCH-009.notes: Working capital efficiency: days of sales tied up in receivables + inventory − payables.

BENCH-010.notes: Revenue per employee from payroll headcount (or entered); compared only within the same currency.

BENCH-011.notes: Project profitability: profit before overheads of tagged projects ÷ their revenue.

BENCH-012.notes: Cash conversion cycle: DSO + days inventory − DPO.

BENCH-013.notes: Explicit consent statement must be ticked; who agreed, when and the consent version are stored and audited.

BENCH-014.notes: Median only with 5+ other participants; quartiles only with 10+.

BENCH-015.notes: Groups below the threshold are suppressed and the next broader group is tried; counts are shown only as bands.

BENCH-016.notes: Only aggregates over other participants are returned; no organisation id in the pool; tests check no single value is returned.

BENCH-017.notes: Rounded ratios under random keys in a system-only pool; no differential-privacy noise yet (differencing over time is a documented limitation).

BENCH-018.notes: Participation is a tenant table with forced RLS; the pool has a system-only RLS policy, tested against tenant reads and writes.

BENCH-019.notes: Formulas, thresholds, peer-group order and privacy rules are shown on the page and in docs/BENCHMARKING.md.

BENCH-020.notes: The live pool holds only real participants; nothing is invented. Demo organisations never reach it.

BENCH-021.notes: Synthetic peers (seed:benchmark-peers, refused in production) are flagged is_synthetic, compared only with demo organisations and labelled on the page.

INNOV-001.notes: Relationship explorer over customers, vendors, invoices, bills, payments, journal entries, accounts, projects, departments, loans, fixed assets and alerts (risks), every connection with a plain-language reason, read live from the books. Contracts are not modelled in the product yet, so they are not in the graph.

INNOV-007.notes: Trial balance, profit and loss and balance sheet lines open the general ledger for the same dates; each ledger line names the record that created it (document, payment, expense claim, pay run, asset, depreciation, deferral, accrual, loan, close adjustment, intercompany charge or the reversed entry) and links to it and to its connections. P&L lines filtered by department or project are not linked because the ledger is not filtered.

INNOV-002.notes: Decisions with context, assumptions and expected outcomes (KPIs with a target and month, compared with the month before the decision and measured from the posted books); search across decisions, assumptions and lessons; review records whether each assumption held, a verdict and lessons, and freezes the measured figures; reviewed and withdrawn decisions are locked by a database trigger. Approved scenarios and recovery plans can be recorded as decisions.

INNOV-009.notes: Eight forecasting methods (last month, 3/6/12-month averages, same month last year, last month plus trend, straight-line trend, exponential smoothing) backtested with a rolling origin over 6, 12 or 18 months on revenue, cost of sales, operating expenses, net income and net cash flow; ranked by WAPE with MAE, bias, within-10% and error by months ahead; saved runs are immutable and their forecasts are measured against the books once each month is over.

INNOV-010.notes: Customer default (write-off of the customer's balance and loss of its share of sales), supplier failure (lost sales until replaced, then a share-weighted cost rise), liquidity shock (frozen cash, withdrawn credit, late payers), operational disruption (lost sales, recovery cost, insurance) and demand collapse, built from the organisation's own customers, suppliers and cash and played through the digital twin; each shock also measured alone; seven standard stress tests ranked worst first; saved simulations re-run on the latest books and can be copied into a twin scenario.

INNOV-003.notes: A policy is written in plain words; the AI (Claude, through the AI control guard and the copilot's switch and budget, prompt version recorded) drafts rules and tests from the words and asks about anything unclear, and the person answers to revise the draft. Nothing the AI proposes is saved or runs until a person saves it and someone else approves it. Live drafting waits on a Claude key (scripted model in tests).

INNOV-004.notes: Each rule is a workflow definition (trigger, conditions, actions to roles or the customer/vendor). Test cases state whether a rule should act on given facts and run on the server, with each condition's actual value; a back-test runs event rules over the last 90 days of real events. Approval needs every test passing and someone other than the last editor (workflows.manage); it creates or versions one workflow per rule and turns off workflows of removed rules. Every version (created, edited, approved, retired) is kept in an immutable table.

INNOV-015.notes: A dashboard is described in words; the AI (Claude, through the AI control guard and the copilot's switch and budget, prompt version recorded) proposes widgets, says what asked-for data is not available, and asks questions that the person answers to revise the draft. Live drafting waits on a Claude key (scripted model in tests).

INNOV-016.notes: Configurations (figure, line, bar, table, top customers) may only use 23 approved metrics (the KPIs and main figures of the books); the engine checks every widget (approved metric, units not mixed in a chart, month and count limits) whether the AI or a person built it, and works out every figure from posted month figures. The AI never produces a number. Customer widgets need sales.read.

INNOV-012.notes: Covered by the financial recovery planner (docs/RECOVERY_PLANNER.md): recovery options measured on the digital twin from the books (collections, supplier terms, cost cuts, funding, pricing), combined into plans with their cash effect and evidence.

INNOV-018.notes: Covered by benchmarking (docs/BENCHMARKING.md): opt-in with recorded consent, an anonymous pool with no organisation id, medians only with 5+ peers and quartiles with 10+, each metric's formula shown for explanation.

INNOV-017.notes: Layouts of headings, fixed text, figures and monthly commentary, drafted by the AI from instructions (through the AI control guard, prompt version recorded) or built by hand. Reports freeze the month's figures; commentary is written from them by the AI (rejected if it quotes a number not in them) or by a person (flagged); final reports are immutable in the database. Live AI waits on a Claude key (scripted model in tests).

INNOV-013.notes: Speak a question (browser Web Speech API, en-IN; Talk2Tax receives only text), stored as VOICE, model told it was spoken; answers to spoken questions read aloud. Tested end to end with test doubles for speech recognition and output; waits on a live Claude key and a real-browser microphone check.

INNOV-014.notes: The copilot can only propose a task or acknowledging/dismissing an alert; the member who asked confirms on screen within 15 minutes (never by speech; sensitive ones ask twice), permission re-checked and the action carried out in the same transaction as the decision; decided actions immutable (trigger); audited.

INNOV-008.notes: Thirteen business changes across sales (new customer, lost customer, prices, salespeople, customer terms), HR (hires, pay rise, headcount reduction), procurement (supplier price by supplier share, supplier terms) and operations (new site, equipment, running costs), built from the books (cost of sales ratio, customers' sales, suppliers' bills) and played through the digital twin against carrying on as is; before/after revenue, margins, operating and net profit and cash; each change on its own with the statement lines it moves and its payback; each business area on its own with interaction; saved assessments re-run on the books; copy to a twin scenario.

INNOV-011.notes: Four kinds found in twelve months of posted books (lapsed customers to win back, revenue lines to cross-sell to active customers, the best-margin department or project, slipped gross margin restored by price), each with named evidence, user-set rates, confidence and reason, measured on the twin via the business impact engine, ranked by extra net profit; every kind that finds nothing says why; an opportunity can be taken forward as a saved impact assessment. Needs reports.read and sales.read.

I18N-001.notes: Each person chooses the interface language (English or Hindi) on Account and preferences; the navigation, header, roles and the preferences page are translated; other pages are still in English and fall back to English text.

I18N-008.notes: Each organisation has a time zone (owners and admins set it, audited) and each person may choose their own; moments (times things happened) are shown in it. Business dates such as today, due dates and periods are still calculated in India time for every organisation.

I18N-011.notes: English text is the key; a catalogue per language maps it, and missing text falls back to English. Tests check that every navigation label is translated, that no two different labels share a translation and that placeholders are kept.

I18N-012.notes: The page direction (dir) comes from the language's metadata, so a right-to-left language can be added; no right-to-left language is offered yet and layouts are not yet mirrored.

I18N-013.notes: English is the default and the source text.

I18N-014.notes: Hindi covers the navigation, header, roles and the preferences page; the rest falls back to English. Translations not yet reviewed by a professional translator.

I18N-015.notes: A language is a catalogue in the web app plus its code in the engine's LANGUAGES list and the database check; formats and time zones are independent of language.

I18N-016.notes: Language and formats are display-only and stored per person; tax and legal behaviour follows the organisation's country and settings, never the interface language. Tax terms and return names stay as the law writes them in every language.

I18N-005.notes: India has its full GST engine. UAE, UK, Singapore, Australia, Germany and Canada have starter modules whose standard national sales-tax rates can be added as ordinary tax rates posting to Output Tax Payable and Input Tax Receivable. The US and other countries are accounting only. No returns, schemes or rule checks outside India.

TAX-042.notes: Each country shows its level (full, starter, accounting only) at onboarding and on the Country module page; India-only pages are hidden elsewhere and the API refuses that work. Nothing claims compliance outside India.

UX-003.notes: Onboarding offers the eight country modules, fills in the usual currency and financial-year start, and shows what Talk2Tax covers in the chosen country before the organisation is created. The country cannot be changed later.

I18N-007.notes: Balance sheet and profit and loss in India Schedule III (Division I), UK Companies Act formats (FRS 102) and IFRS IAS 1 layouts, chosen by country, with the year before, the accounts behind each line, and accounts without a subtype flagged. Presentation only: no notes, cash flow statement, Ind AS (Division II), rounding to lakhs or crores, or MCA/Companies House filing.

ENT-028.notes: Presentation layouts for Schedule III (AS), UK Companies Act/FRS 102 and IFRS IAS 1 over one ledger. Recognition and measurement do not differ by framework: there are no framework-specific adjustments, Ind AS or US GAAP.

GL-035.notes: Period-end revaluation of monetary foreign-currency balances (cash, receivables, payables, loans, accruals) at recorded or entered closing rates; unrealised gain or loss posted to the FX_GAIN_LOSS account and reversed the next day; immutable records. Inventory, prepayments and fixed assets stay at historical rates.

TRS-013.notes: Exchange rates page shows foreign-currency balances by account and currency at any date, carried and at a chosen rate, and the gain or loss a revaluation would post. No sensitivity ranges or hedging.

PERF-007.notes: One deployment per region (DEPLOYMENT_REGION); organisations tagged with their data region at creation and served only there (421 WRONG_REGION elsewhere, with a link to the home region); audited operator move command. Implemented, not Production ready: no second region is running, and the data copy during a move is a manual database step.

ADMIN-001.notes: A dedicated platform administration area (/admin) of the web app with its own layout and API (/v1/admin), for people with a platform role (SUPER_ADMIN, SUPPORT); first administrator via the admin:grant command.

ADMIN-002.notes: Tenants (organisations) listed and searched by name, member email or id, with country, region, members, owners and status; overview counts.

ADMIN-003.notes: Organisation detail (metadata and members only), suspension with a reason shown to members (read-only, 423 ORG_SUSPENDED on changes) and reinstatement, written to the organisation's own audit trail.

ADMIN-019.notes: Announcements with tone, start and optional end, withdrawn early if needed, shown on every page to everyone signed in.

ADMIN-021.notes: Platform roles never grant organisation routes (membership still required, 404 otherwise); admin views select metadata columns only; tested that a super admin gets 404 on an organisation's accounts and journals. Since M9 slice 4 the one exception is support access the organisation grants itself (ADMIN-022): read-only, time-limited and logged.

SUBS-011.notes: Plans (prices per currency and interval, limits, modules, offered flag, order) edited by super admins, validated and audited.

SUBS-012.notes: Monthly billing periods (calendar month, end of month kept).

SUBS-013.notes: Annual billing periods at ten months' price.

SUBS-014.notes: 14-day trial (PLAN_TRIAL_DAYS) of every module for new organisations; admins extend trials; read-only (not locked) when it ends.

SUBS-015.notes: Upgrades in a paid period are charged online for the days left (upgradeCharge) and take effect on payment; the period end is kept.

SUBS-023.notes: Enterprise contracts activated by an administrator with the contract reference, or invoiced and paid by transfer (recorded under Invoices); no contract terms or custom prices yet.

SUBS-026.notes: INR prices for organisations in India and USD elsewhere, per plan.

SUBS-032.notes: Subscriptions in their own tables and history, never posted to an organisation's books; the page says so.

ADMIN-005.notes: Subscriptions in Platform administration: filter, activate with payment reference, extend trials, cancel, complimentary.

SUBS-027.notes: GST on subscription invoices from an Indian supplier with a GSTIN: CGST+SGST in the same state (or state unknown), IGST in another state, zero-rated export outside India. No tax computed for a supplier outside India.

SUBS-028.notes: Renewal invoices are issued automatically 7 days before the period ends and paid by the customer (online or by transfer). Cards and UPI AutoPay are not charged automatically.

SUBS-029.notes: Unpaid renewals go to 7 days grace, then read-only; a wrong amount or a payment on a replaced invoice is recorded and not applied; a cancelled payment can be retried; a late renewal starts from the day paid.

SUBS-030.notes: Reminders once per invoice and stage (upcoming, due, final, lapsed), emailed to owners and admins through the organisation’s email set-up, and recorded in the subscription history.

SUBS-031.notes: Payment request while unpaid; tax invoice numbered on payment (PREFIX/YY-YY/NNNNN, at most 16 characters, a series per financial year); printable; final once paid or void.

INTG-009.notes: Razorpay Payment Links and webhooks, set up in Platform admin → Payments. Tested against a local stand-in of the API; needs a check with real Razorpay test keys.

INTG-007.notes: Stripe Checkout Sessions and webhooks, set up in Platform admin → Payments. Tested against a local stand-in of the API; needs a check with real Stripe test keys.

ADMIN-015.notes: Platform admin → Invoices (all subscription invoices, record a payment by hand, void, ask the gateway, issue due renewals, gateway notices) and → Payments (gateways and seller details).

ADMIN-012.notes: Tickets with topic and urgency, first-answer and resolution targets by urgency (1h/8h urgent to 72h/7d low, clock hours), a queue ordered by whose turn it is and the nearest target, assignment, internal notes never shown to the customer, replies emailed through the organisation's mail set-up, append-only messages, every status change in the organisation's audit chain.

ADMIN-022.notes: Only an owner or admin can grant; 1 to 72 hours with a reason, optionally tied to a ticket; one grant at a time; revocable; support staff get viewer rights for GET requests only (writes 403 SUPPORT_READ_ONLY); every request logged in an append-only table the organisation sees; grants can only be revoked once (database trigger).

NAV-044.notes: Help and support in the Governance group (and for staff who only claim expenses).

SUBS-018.notes: Each plan's monthly AI requests are metered (one per answered model call, any agent, own key or Talk2Tax's) and enforced before every model call (429 AI_CREDITS_USED_UP). Buying extra credits beyond the plan is not built.

SUBS-019.notes: Each plan's monthly uploads are counted per stored attachment and enforced inside the upload's transaction under a per-organisation lock (429 UPLOAD_LIMIT_REACHED); refused and duplicate files are not counted.

ADMIN-008.notes: Platform admin → Usage: AI requests and tokens and uploads per organisation per month against each plan, fullest first, with totals and organisations at or near a limit.

ADMIN-007.notes: Flags declared in code with defaults; administrators switch one off for everyone, roll it out to a stable hashed share of organisations, or set it for one organisation (kept in that organisation's audit trail). The API refuses a switched-off module with 403 FEATURE_OFF and the menu hides it. Four modules are behind flags so far.

ADMIN-010.notes: Requests per route pattern over the last 15 minutes: counts, 4xx and 5xx, p50 and p95, and requests per minute. In memory per API server instance; not aggregated across instances.

ADMIN-011.notes: System health measured on request: database latency, size, connections, PostgreSQL version and migrations; API version, uptime, memory and load; each background runner's last pass, duration, failures and lateness. No external metrics system or alerting to an on-call service yet.

ADMIN-017.notes: Every unexpected 5xx is recorded with its request id (shown to the person as a reference), grouped by error kind, code location and route; findable by reference; resolve and reopen; a resolved group that recurs opens again. Occurrences kept 30 days. Errors in the web app's browser code are not collected yet.

ADMIN-020.notes: Start now or schedule a maintenance window with a message and expected end. While in progress every change by anyone but platform staff is refused (503 MAINTENANCE with Retry-After); reads, sign-in and payment webhooks keep working, background runners skip their passes, and a banner shows on every page including sign-in.

SEC-025.notes: pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high as a CI job, and weekly Dependabot updates for npm, GitHub Actions and base images. Four high-severity transitive advisories fixed with pinned overrides (audit clean locally). The CI job has not run on GitHub because Actions is blocked by billing.

CRM-003.notes: Leads LD-0001 with source, owner (a member), estimated value; NEW/CONTACTED/QUALIFIED/DISQUALIFIED (reason required, reopenable); duplicate warning by email against leads and contacts; converted once into a new or existing customer (a vendor becomes a customer too), optionally with a deal. Never deleted; a converted lead is frozen by a trigger; append-only activity timeline (calls, emails, meetings, notes, every change).

CRM-004.notes: Deals DL-0001 for a customer through PROSPECTING/QUALIFICATION/PROPOSAL/NEGOTIATION to WON (100%) or LOST (0%, reason required), reopenable; default stage probabilities overridable; weighted value; board by stage, overdue deals, 90-day win rate and days to win, weighted value by expected close month; deals on the customer page. Single currency (functional) for now.

CRM-001.notes: Native lightweight CRM (leads, pipeline, quotations, orders, contracts, customer 360, revenue forecast) and integration APIs for external CRMs: API keys made under Settings > Integrations (hashed, scoped read/write, expiry, revoke, act as their creator), the CRM API at /v1/crm-api (also /api/crm on the app) with idempotent creation by externalRef, and signed CRM webhooks from the audit trail with retries, test, delivery log and secret rotation.

CRM-005.notes: Quotations QT-0001 with the invoice tax rules (tax rates, GST place of supply, HSN/SAC); draft (editable, deletable) -> sent (frozen by a trigger) -> accepted or declined (reason); expired past valid-until; revisions QT-0001-R2 supersede the previous one when sent; linked to a deal, which is won on acceptance; acceptance rate on the list. No PDF or e-mail of a quotation yet.

CRM-007.notes: Sales orders SO-0001 from an accepted quotation or entered directly with the customer's PO; lines and prices never change (trigger); open/partly billed/billed; cancel with a reason only while nothing is billed; entering one for a deal wins the deal.

CRM-008.notes: Bill an order in full or by chosen quantities into a draft invoice (reference SO-0001 / customer PO) built by the normal invoice rules; billed quantities count while the invoice is draft or posted and are freed when it is voided or the draft deleted; over-billing refused under a row lock.

CRM-006.notes: Customer contracts CT-0001: monthly/quarterly/half-yearly/yearly, in advance or arrears, fixed end on a period end or rolling; draft -> active <-> paused -> ended/cancelled; renew by hand (with % price change) or automatically; renewal-due flag from notice days; MRR/ARR; append-only history; activating for a deal wins it.

AR-010.notes: Each due contract period becomes a draft invoice (invoice rules incl. GST), by the background runner (CONTRACT_RUNNER_INTERVAL_SECONDS), on activation, Bill now, or Bill due periods now; each period recorded once (no double billing); deleted/voided invoice can be billed again; failures kept on the contract and retried. Invoices are drafts to check and post; no auto-posting or auto-email yet.

AR-029.notes: Contract billing from the contract's lines in force on the billing day; price changes and renewals apply to later periods only; reference CT-0001 <period> / customer reference.

AR-011.notes: Fixed-fee recurring billing works through contracts (CRM-006/AR-010). Not built: usage-based or metered charges, proration of part periods, card/mandate auto-collection.

CRM-010.notes: Customer profitability: revenue (income lines of posted invoices less credit notes) less direct costs (expenses posted to the customer's linked projects), monthly for 12 months and to date; ranked on Customer insights.

CRM-011.notes: Lifetime value = gross profit to date + yearly gross profit (max of trailing 12m revenue and contract ARR, at the customer's margin) x expected years r/(1-r) (max 5) from the org's own 12-month retention; 3 years assumed (and shown) with fewer than 5 customers to measure.

CRM-012.notes: Credit risk score 0-100 from 5 explained factors (overdue share, oldest overdue, days late, limit use, slowing), ratings low/medium/high/very high, suggested credit limit, credit hold that blocks invoice posting with audit trail.

CRM-013.notes: Deterministic forecast by month from active contracts (by invoice date, auto-renew runs on), open orders (left to bill, this month), open deals (weighted/full at close month) and the 3-month run rate of other sales; committed/expected/best; itemised; saved forecasts RF-0001 (immutable) compared with actual revenue (WAPE). AI explanation not built yet.

INTG-025.notes: Any CRM platform can connect through the generic CRM API (API keys) and CRM webhooks. Ready-made connectors for named platforms (Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho) that map their objects automatically are not built.

AR-031.notes: Invoices, credit notes, bills, vendor credits, receipts and payments in any supported currency, at the recorded rate on the date or one entered and kept with the record. Settling at another rate posts a realised exchange gain or loss (reversed if the allocation is removed). Receivables and payables, ageing, balances, credit limits and approvals are in the functional currency at each record's rate; customer statements are per currency. Not yet: TDS/TCS, reverse charge or GST charged on foreign-currency documents, e-invoices for them, quotations/orders/contracts in other currencies, rate feeds.

BANK-012.notes: Receipts and payments in a foreign currency into any bank account, realised gains and losses on settlement and period-end revaluation of foreign balances. Bank statement import and reconciliation are still in the functional currency only.

DS-012.notes: Currency and exchange-rate picker on invoices, bills, credits and payments: shows the recorded rate on the date and the home-currency amount.

GL-012.notes: Templates with lines (any currency, departments, projects), memo, reference and placeholders such as {month}; used by hand as a draft or posted, saved from any manual journal, archived once used.

GL-007.notes: Template schedules monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly, on the start day or the month's last day, to an end date or until ended; each run a draft or a posted Recurring journal, made once (numbered, in one transaction), by the hourly runner or Run due now; failures kept and retried; pause, resume (catch up or skip), end. Not yet: weekly or custom calendars, auto-reversing templates.

AR-026.notes: Provision matrix from the receivables ageing (rate per bucket, editable), specific provisions for invoices marked doubtful at their own percentage, foreign invoices at their own rate; each provision posts only the difference from the allowance in the books (increase or release) as a BAD_DEBT journal, kept append-only with the matrix it used. Not yet: provision rates learnt from history (expected-credit-loss model), provisions per customer group.

AR-027.notes: Write off all or part of a posted invoice against the allowance (refused beyond what it holds) or straight to bad-debt expense, at the invoice's own exchange rate; settles the invoice like a receipt, so ageing, statement and control account agree, without changing GST returns or e-invoices; reversible once (journal and settlement reversed). Not yet: GST bad-debt relief, write-offs of payables or small balances in bulk.

GL-011.notes: Year-end close: revenue and expense accounts closed to a chosen retained earnings account by a CLOSING journal (YE-) on the year's last day, previewed line by line; closing again posts only what changed; reopening reverses the closes. Profit-and-loss reports, KPIs, budgets, dimensions, CFO, recovery and month-end checks leave CLOSING journals out; balance sheet and trial balance include them. Not yet: closing by department or project, automatic lock after closing.

AP-014.notes: Payment batches PB-0001: draft (bills, part payments) -> approved by someone other than the preparer (self-approval only when no one else can approve, flagged) -> bank file CSV (beneficiary, account, IFSC, amount, reference) -> payments recorded, one per vendor, settling the bills; cancel with a reason. A bill is in one open batch at most; approved batches are frozen by a trigger. Functional currency only; no direct bank API (H2H) upload yet.

AP-027.notes: Vendor bank details (account holder, number, IFSC) with an append-only masked change history; any change clears verification in the database; verification needs approvals.decide and someone other than the person who changed them (unless no one else can); batches with unverified or changed details cannot be approved, sent to the bank or paid.

AR-005.notes: Same feature as CRM-005: Quotations QT-0001 with the invoice tax rules (tax rates, GST place of supply, HSN/SAC); draft (editable, deletable) -> sent (frozen by a trigger) -> accepted or declined (reason); expired past valid-until; revisions QT-0001-R2 supersede the previous one when sent; linked to a deal, which is won on acceptance; acceptance rate on the list. No PDF or e-mail of a quotation yet.

AR-007.notes: Same feature as CRM-007: Sales orders SO-0001 from an accepted quotation or entered directly with the customer's PO; lines and prices never change (trigger); open/partly billed/billed; cancel with a reason only while nothing is billed; entering one for a deal wins the deal.

AR-017.notes: Debit notes DN-000001: an INVOICE linked to an earlier posted invoice (same customer, currency, place of supply, not before it); owed, aged and paid like an invoice; GSTR-1 9B type D with the original number, table 13 own series, GSTR-3B outward tax, e-invoice DBN, print titled Debit note with Against invoice. Invoice cannot be voided while a debit note stands (trigger). Sales side only.

AP-005.notes: Recurring bills RB-0001: vendor, lines (GST rate, SAC, dimensions), place of supply, reverse charge, TDS section, due days; monthly/quarterly/half-yearly/yearly schedule (month end, end date) that makes each due run as a draft or posted bill through the normal bill code (GST, TDS, approval rules, periods, duplicate vendor reference). The vendor reference must carry a placeholder that changes each run. The first bill is checked on save inside a rolled-back savepoint. Runs recorded once in the same transaction (append-only); failures kept on the schedule; pause/resume (skip missed)/end; Make recurring from a bill. Hourly runner (RECURRING_BILL_RUNNER_INTERVAL_SECONDS). Functional currency only.

AP-007.notes: Payment schedule: each open bill gets a planned pay date and optional part amount (bill_payment_plans, bills only by trigger); suggested date = due date or the last chosen pay weekday before it, never the past; plans checked (not past, not before bill date, not more than left); weekly planned outflows against ledger bank balances with short weeks flagged (receipts not included); Plan the rest auto-plans unplanned bills; Prepare batch takes bills planned up to a date into a new payment batch with their amounts; Plan payment… from a bill. Functional currency only; planning moves no money.

AR-025.notes: Invoice disputes DS-0001: raised from a posted invoice with something due, for part or all of what is due (checked), with reason, description, owner (a member) and target date; one open per invoice (partial unique index); changes and notes kept in an append-only history; resolved by a posted credit note of the same customer and currency, customer pays, written off or withdrawn, then final (trigger). An open dispute keeps the invoice out of AI payment reminders and the INVOICE_OVERDUE workflow trigger; it still counts in receivables. Summary: open count and amount, past target, oldest, average days to settle, outcomes.

AR-008.notes: Pro forma invoices PF-0001: drafted directly or from a sent/accepted quotation, lines worked out by the invoice rules (GST place of supply); issued then fixed (DB trigger on header and lines); printed with the invoice template as PRO_FORMA (heading Pro forma invoice, Not a tax invoice, Valid until); Make tax invoice creates a draft invoice with the same lines referenced PF-0001, deleting/voiding it frees the pro forma; cancel with reason; posts nothing. Functional currency only; advance via an ordinary receipt applied to the tax invoice.

AP-015.notes: Purchase orders PO-0001: drafted with lines worked out by the bill rules (GST vendor state/place of supply), expected date (late flag), match mode two-way/three-way and price/quantity tolerances; issued then fixed (DB trigger on header and lines); close with reason (short close) or cancel when nothing received/billed; Make bill drafts a bill for what is left to bill; bill lines keep purchase_order_line_id through edits; two-way matching checks price and quantity ordered. Functional currency only.

AP-016.notes: Goods receipts GRN-0001 against issued three-way orders: date, delivery note, accepted and rejected quantity per line with note; over-receipt refused beyond the quantity tolerance; never edited or deleted (DB triggers), cancelled with a reason unless bills rely on the quantity. Does not move stock.

AP-017.notes: Three-way matching of bills against order and goods received: exceptions for price above order (+tolerance), more than ordered, more than received (+tolerance), lines not on the order, order closed/cancelled; several bill lines per order line add up with other non-void bills; posting refused (409 BILL_MATCH_EXCEPTION) until approvals.decide accepts the exact differences with a reason (fingerprinted, append-only, audit); Purchase order match panel on the bill page.
